title: Global-sections cup and evaluation comparison on shifted derived Hom
statement:
Let $(\mathcal C,\mathcal O)$ be a ringed site small in the module universe [def-weil-size-convention, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], with $\mathcal O$ a sheaf of commutative rings. Let $A$ be a commutative ring with a ring homomorphism $A\to\Gamma(\mathcal C,\mathcal O)$. The resulting ringed-topos morphism [def-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-morphism] $p:(\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C),\mathcal O)\to(\operatorname{Set},A)$ has module direct image the global-sections functor with this $A$-action. Present $\operatorname{Set}$ by the one-object site with only its identity and the maximal covering sieve. Use ordinary unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], K-flat derived tensor, K-injective derived global sections $G=Rp_*:D(\mathcal O)\to D(A)$ [def-pur-ringed-site-zeroth-hypercohomology], and internal Hom $H=R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O}$ [def-pur-derived-internal-hom], with evaluation and the tensor-Hom adjunction [lem-sf-ringed-derived-closed-symmetric-monoidal]. Let $Lp^*:D(A)\to D(\mathcal O)$ be the derived module pullback, computed on K-flat resolutions with flat terms, with its canonical tensor comparison $Lp^*(P\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}Q)\cong Lp^*P\otimes_{\mathcal O}^{\mathbf L}Lp^*Q$ [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback], and let $Lp^*\dashv G$ be the derived adjunction obtained from the module adjunction $p^*\dashv p_*$ [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-adjunction] by [lem-pc-pre-derived-adjoint-functors-general], with counit $Lp^*G\to\mathrm{id}$. Define the relative cup product $c_{K,L}:G(K)\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}G(L)\to G(K\otimes_{\mathcal O}^{\mathbf L}L)$ as the adjoint of the tensor of the two counits $Lp^*G(K)\to K$, $Lp^*G(L)\to L$, precomposed with this tensor comparison. For every $L,M\in D(\mathcal O)$ the pairing $G(H(L,M))\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}G(L)\xrightarrow{c}G(H(L,M)\otimes_{\mathcal O}^{\mathbf L}L)\xrightarrow{G(\mathrm{ev})}G(M)$ has a transpose
$$\chi_{L,M}:G(H(L,M))\longrightarrow R\operatorname{Hom}_A(G(L),G(M)),$$
natural contravariantly in $L$ and covariantly in $M$. There are canonical identifications $H^nG(H(L,M))\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathcal O)}(L,M[n])$ and $H^nR\operatorname{Hom}_A(G(L),G(M))\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{D(A)}(G(L),G(M)[n])$. Under these identifications $H^n(\chi_{L,M})$ sends $u:L\to M[n]$ to $G(u):G(L)\to G(M[n])\cong G(M)[n]$, using the canonical derived shift comparison, for every integer $n$. No boundedness, quasi-coherence, perfectness or invertibility of $\chi_{L,M}$ is assumed.

source.place: Tags 0B6C (remark-cup-product) and 0B6D (remark-projection-formula-for-internal-hom), specialized to the global-sections ringed-topos morphism; Tag 08JA (lemma-section-RHom-over-U), including its K-flat/K-injective proof, gives the shifted Hom identifications. The normalization follows by the two tensor-adjunction triangles.

proof.text: Write $F=Lp^*$, $T=H(L,M)$, $e:T\otimes^{\mathbf L}L\to M$, and $\varepsilon:FG\to1$. Let $t_{X,Y}:F(X\otimes^{\mathbf L}Y)\cong FX\otimes^{\mathbf L}FY$ be the specified canonical comparison. By [lem-weil-pbc-pullback-tensor-canonical-shift-unit] its unit comparison $j_0:F(A)\cong\mathcal O$ and integer-shift comparisons give $j_n:F(A[-n])\cong\mathcal O[-n]$, compatible with $t$ and the shifted left unitors. By [lem-weil-pbc-derived-adjunction-shift] the canonical shifts of $F,G$ make $\varepsilon$ shift-compatible. These results apply to the specified one-object target site and to an arbitrary structural ring map; they impose neither flatness of $A\to\Gamma(\mathcal O)$ nor boundedness.

source.place: Tag 07A4, lemma-pullback-tensor-product; canonical unit and shift normalization on flat-term K-flat representatives; derived.tex Tag 05SU, lemma-derived-shift.

proof.text: By definition and the inverse adjunction formula [lem-weil-pbc-adjunction-of-natural-bijection], $\varepsilon_{K\otimes L}F(c_{K,L})=(\varepsilon_K\otimes\varepsilon_L)t_{GK,GL}$. Put $B=G(e)c_{T,L}:GT\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}GL\to GM$. Apply [lem-sf-ringed-derived-closed-symmetric-monoidal] to the one-object ringed site $(\operatorname{Set},A)$: its closed adjunction transposes $B$ to $\chi:GT\to R\operatorname{Hom}_A(GL,GM)$. Naturality follows explicitly as follows. For $r:L'\to L$ and $s:M\to M'$, evaluation satisfies $e_{L',M'}(H(r,s)\otimes1)=s\,e_{L,M}(1\otimes r)$. Tensor comparison and counit naturality, then injectivity of the adjunction bijection, give naturality of $c$. Applying $G$ to the evaluation equation and using that naturality gives $B_{L',M'}(GH(r,s)\otimes1)=G(s)B_{L,M}(1\otimes G(r))$. Closed transposition is natural, proving the stated variance of $\chi$.

The existing unbounded model [lem-sfb-derived-internal-hom-sections-model], applied to $(\mathcal C,\mathcal O)$, gives $H^nG(T)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(L,M[n])$. Applied to the one-object site with coefficient ring $A$, it gives $H^nR\operatorname{Hom}_A(GL,GM)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(GL,GM[n])$. For any $Y\in D(A)$, [lem-sc-module-cup-homology-representability] also identifies a class in $H^nY$ with a map $A[-n]\to Y$, naturally in $Y$; on a representative complex this takes a degree-$n$ cocycle to the chain map sending $1$ to that cocycle. All maps in the global Hom model respect the $A$-action termwise, so its underlying abelian-group cohomology identifications are the ones for the stated $A$-valued $G$.

source.place: Tag 08JA, lemma-section-RHom-over-U, including its Hom-complex computation; shifted free-module cocycle evaluation.

proof.text: Fix $n\in\mathbf Z$. Choose a flat-term K-flat representative $P$ of $L$ and a K-injective representative $I$ of $M$, using [lem-pc-kflat-resolution, prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist]. The sheaf complex $\mathcal Hom^\bullet(P,I)$ represents $T$ and is K-injective by [lem-pur-hom-kflat-into-kinjective]. The sections model [lem-sfb-derived-internal-hom-sections-model] represents $GT$ by the $A$-complex $C=\operatorname{Hom}^\bullet(P,I)$. Thus a class $u:L\to M[n]$ is represented by a degree-$n$ cocycle $\phi$ in $C$, and the corresponding $x:S=A[-n]\to GT$ is represented by $1\mapsto\phi$, by [lem-sc-module-cup-homology-representability]. No K-injectivity of the section complex $C$ is asserted or needed.

source.place: Tag 08JA, lemma-section-RHom-over-U, proof; its K-flat and K-injective choices and global Hom-complex representative.

proof.text:
Set $a=\varepsilon_TF(x)j_n^{-1}:\mathcal O[-n]\to T$. The resolution-normalization statement [lem-sfb-resolving-derived-adjunction-normalization] computes its adjunction on the K-flat source $S$ and K-injective target $\mathcal Hom^\bullet(P,I)$. The ordinary module adjunction [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-adjunction] takes $1\mapsto\phi$ to the sheaf map $r\mapsto r\phi$ from $\mathcal O[-n]$. The canonical componentwise uncurrying in [lem-sf-ringed-derived-tensor-hom-adjunction] therefore makes $e(a\otimes1_L)$ the localization of the chain map $P[-n]\to I$, $z\mapsto\phi(z)$, after the shifted left unitor. Write $d_Z:\mathcal O[-n]\otimes^{\mathbf L}Z\cong Z[-n]$ for that unitor/shift comparison. It follows that
$$v=e(a\otimes1_L)d_L^{-1}:L[-n]\to M$$
is precisely $u[-n]$, under the canonical shift-addition identifications: both are the map represented by the same Hom cocycle $\phi$. This proves the normalization, rather than assuming it from an unspecified cohomology isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 08J9, lemma-internal-hom, componentwise tensor-Hom adjunction; derived.tex lemma-derived-adjoint-functors and its resolving-representative normalization.

proof.text:
Uncurrying $\chi x$ in $D(A)$ gives $b=B(x\otimes1_{GL}):S\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}GL\to GM$. Its $F\dashv G$-transpose is
$$w=\varepsilon_MF(b)=e(\varepsilon_T\otimes\varepsilon_L)t_{GT,GL}F(x\otimes1)=e((\varepsilon_TF(x))\otimes\varepsilon_L)t_{S,GL}.$$
The first equality is the inverse adjunction formula. For the second use counit naturality for $e$ and the defining counit equation for $c$ in step 2. The third is naturality of $t$. Every arrow is defined for the unbounded objects in question. In particular the tensor factors remain in their original order; no symmetry is inserted.

source.place: Tags 0B6C and 0B6D, expansion of the two adjunction transposes.

proof.text:
Let $d'_Y:S\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}Y\cong Y[-n]$ be the point-site version of $d$. Write $\sigma^F_Y:F(Y[-n])\cong FY[-n]$ and $\sigma^G_Z:G(Z[-n])\cong GZ[-n]$. The shifted-unit coherence from step 1 gives
$$(j_n\otimes1)t_{S,GL}F((d'_{GL})^{-1})=d_{FGL}^{-1}\sigma^F_{GL}.$$
Substitute $\varepsilon_TF(x)=a j_n$ in step 6. Naturality of $d$ for $\varepsilon_L:FGL\to L$, followed by step 5, then gives
$$wF((d'_{GL})^{-1})=v\,\varepsilon_L[-n]\,\sigma^F_{GL}.$$
On the other hand the adjoint of $G(v)(\sigma^G_L)^{-1}:GL[-n]\to GM$ is
$$\varepsilon_MF(G(v))F((\sigma^G_L)^{-1})=v\varepsilon_{L[-n]}F((\sigma^G_L)^{-1})=v\varepsilon_L[-n]\sigma^F_{GL}.$$
Here the first simplification is counit naturality and the last is exactly the counit/shift equation of [lem-weil-pbc-derived-adjunction-shift]. Injectivity of the adjunction bijection proves $b(d'_{GL})^{-1}=G(v)(\sigma^G_L)^{-1}$.

source.place: Tags 07A4 and 0B6D; tensor/unit/shift coherence and the derived-adjunction triangles.

proof.text: Run steps 4–5 on the one-object site $(\operatorname{Set},A)$, where $F=G=\mathrm{id}$. Choose a flat-term K-flat representative $P'$ of $GL$ and a K-injective representative $I'$ of $GM$ [lem-pc-kflat-resolution, prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist]; $R\operatorname{Hom}_A(GL,GM)$ is represented by $\operatorname{Hom}^\bullet(P',I')$, which is its own global sections [lem-sfb-derived-internal-hom-sections-model]. By [lem-sc-module-cup-homology-representability] the class of $\chi x$ in $H^n$ is that of a degree-$n$ cocycle $\psi$ with $\chi x$ represented by $1\mapsto\psi$. The closed adjunction [lem-sf-ringed-derived-closed-symmetric-monoidal] gives $b=B(x\otimes1)=e'(\chi x\otimes1_{GL})$, and the componentwise uncurrying of [lem-sf-ringed-derived-tensor-hom-adjunction] represents it by $1\otimes z\mapsto\psi(z)$; with the sign-free first-input unitor $d'$ (as in step 5) $b(d'_{GL})^{-1}$ is the chain map $P'[-n]\to I'$, $z\mapsto\psi(z)$, i.e. the shift by $-n$ of the map $GL\to GM[n]$ that $\psi$ represents. So the second identification of step 3 takes the class of $\chi x$ to the shift by $n$ of $b(d'_{GL})^{-1}$. Step 7 identifies this with the shift by $n$ of $G(v)(\sigma^G_L)^{-1}$. Since $v=u[-n]$, naturality of $\sigma^G$ and the zero and addition laws of the canonical derived shift comparisons (step 1) identify the latter with $G(u):GL\to G(M[n])\cong GM[n]$. Therefore $H^n(\chi)$ has exactly the claimed action for every integer $n$. The constructions also cover zero objects, $n=0$, and negative $n$; no inversion of $\chi$ or extra finiteness hypothesis has entered.
